AI agents move deeper into chip design; China doubles down on AI compute and memory; chip supply chains tighten for equipment and critical materials; TSMC partners accelerate; ICs head to space; optics advances, neural super resolution, auto PQC; Purdue-UIUC workforce training.

September 25th, 2026 -

By: The SE Staff

AI moves deeper into chip design

Cadence released a new agent for spec-to-RTL generation and early PPA optimization as part of its ChipStack AI Super Agent, reporting about 24% lower area and 18% lower power versus pure foundation model code generation.
The release is part of a broader move toward specialized AI agents across chip-design workflows, which is creating new challenges around orchestration, integration and guardrails. It’s also putting more emphasis on evidence-driven automation, where AI-generated results still need to be verified before sign-off.

AI innovations

Alibaba unveiled its Zhenwu V900 AI accelerator, with 216GB of memory and 1,200GB/s inter-chip bandwidth. Alibaba says the chip delivers 3× the performance of its M890 predecessor, with mass production planned for Q1 2027. The launch expands China’s domestic options for large-scale AI training and inference amid tighter access to leading U.S. chips.
Imagination published the first performance data for its E-Series GPU IP and introduced Neural Super Resolution, combining graphics, compute and AI on one programmable architecture.

Fig. 1: Schematic of accelerator archipelago vs. converged GPU. Source: Imagination Technologies
Memory
China expands memory ambitions

CXMT announced that its fifth-gen G5 DRAM technology entered mass production, along with a new LPDDR5X product line. The company says the process reaches an 11.95nm active-area half-pitch and yields at least 50% more dies per wafer than its previous generation, though it did not disclose actual manufacturing yields.
CXMT is also preparing an R&D production line for NAND flash in Beijing, according to Reuters, potentially expanding the DRAM maker into a market led domestically by YMTC.

YMTC reportedly could begin LPDDR5 trial production as early as year-end, expanding the NAND maker into DRAM as the two Chinese memory companies move into each other’s traditional markets.

HBM and AI memory

Samsung reportedly plans to at least double HBM4-family output in 2027, according to Seoul Economic Daily.
GUC said its HBM4E PHY and controller are design-ready on TSMC N2P and have already been adopted in customer AI ASICs.
Imec researchers modeled a 3D DRAM-on-GPU architecture with vertically oriented DRAM dies and cooling cavities. Simulations cut peak temperature from 121.7°C to 103.4°C versus an HBM-on-GPU baseline, while bandwidth scaled with active DRAM dies.

Chip policy and supply chains

SIA says China is targeting 80% chip self-sufficiency by 2030, requiring chipmakers to use at least 50% domestic semiconductor manufacturing equipment and giving qualifying domestic products a 20% price advantage in government procurement. SIA urged U.S. officials to address those barriers through negotiations and coordinated action with allies.
Chinese authorities are reviewing the use of Broadcom networking technology in state-controlled data centers in keeping with a push to reduce reliance on foreign technology, reports the Financial Times.
The US Commerce Department issued a temporary rule restricting stockpiling of polysilicon and its derivatives ahead of new Section 232 import measures, which take effect on Dec. 4.
ASML is currently selling no chipmaking machines in Europe, according to EVP Frank Heemskerk, who cited insufficient investment and a lack of new fabs. He warned that Europe risks falling further behind as the U.S., China, and India expand domestic chip production.
US and Japanese officials met to discuss yttrium and permanent-magnet supply bottlenecks as Chinese export controls continue to constrain critical-material supplies. Yttrium is used in heat-resistant coatings for chip manufacturing equipment. Chinese customs data showed no U.S.-bound shipments in January, May or June.

TSMC ecosystem developments
At the TSMC 2026 North America OIP Ecosystem Forum in Santa Clara, several ecosystem partners announced expanded collaborations:

Siemens and TSMC introduced an AI agent for automated design rule check fixing across IC flows.
Synopsys and TSMC are extending their work across advanced-node design and packaging, including certified digital and analog EDA flows for TSMC’s A14 process and new agentic AI workflows for analog, digital, and multi-die designs. The companies also extended support for integrated voltage regulators on CoWoS and co-packaged optics.
Cadence demonstrated a UALink solution in N3P, introduced new Si-proven IP for N3P and N2P, and achieved tool certification for TSMC’s A14 process.
AlChip and Synopsys demonstrated a 224G SerDes implementation for AI accelerators.
IC-Link by imec joined TSMC’s OIP Cloud Alliance to expand customer access to advanced-node chip design infrastructure and support.

At the leading edge

ETH Zurich researchers created light-emitting photoresists that can be patterned with UV or electron beams, producing fluorescent features down to 110 nm and OLEDs with 13.3% peak EQE.
Carnegie Mellon-led researchers fabricated wafer-scale monolayer MoS₂ transistors with physical channel lengths below 5 nm using CMOS-compatible photolithography.
Imec developed a 100 GHz Ge/Si avalanche photodiode, demonstrating what it claims is the first net 400 Gbps optical link using an APD receiver, targeting AI data-center interconnects.
Infleqtion demonstrated 30 entangled logical qubits using 80 physical neutral-atom qubits on its Sqale QPU, with a distance-2 code that detects errors and corrects atom loss.

Noteworthy deals and funding

RealSense, the former Intel depth-sensing and 3D-vision business, will be acquired by Cognex for $500M, expanding its reach into robotic perception and physical AI.
Qualcomm agreed to acquire PickNik, developer and steward of the open-source MoveIt robotics-manipulation framework.
PicoJool raised $27.5M to commercialize its 200G VCSEL and MicroVCSEL technology for AI optical interconnects.

Global
Europe

Arm joined the European Chips Design Platform as its first commercial IP provider, giving European startups, SMEs, and research teams access to Arm IP, tools, training, and design support through Arm Flexible Access.
Germany’s SPRIND and the Netherlands’ NADI launched a 20-month competition aimed at using AI for architecture search, RTL generation and verification to shorten chip-development cycles from years to weeks.
In Switzerland, SEALSQ, and WISeKey plan to establish a Post-Quantum Semiconductor and Cybersecurity Center in the Canton of Jura.

Asia

Taiwan broke ground on the Baipu Industrial Park in Kaohsiung, which will include the country’s first testing and validation base dedicated to advanced semiconductor equipment and materials.
Thailand approved its first national semiconductor and advanced electronics strategy, targeting about $80B in cumulative investment and $150B in annual industry revenue by 2050.

Americas

Michigan State University received a $20M NSF grant to build a national user facility focused on diamond and other carbon-based semiconductor materials and devices. The facility will support research into electronics designed to operate in extreme environments, including space, nuclear reactors and high-power systems.
Texas Governor Greg Abbott halted all permits for data centers until state audits are completed.

Reports and Deals
More deals and partnerships

AT&S and Marvell signed a deal to increase advanced IC substrate capacity for AI and cloud infrastructure.
SMART Photonics and GF are developing an open-access foundry service that combines GF silicon photonics with SMART Photonics’ indium-phosphide lasers and optical amplifiers.
GS Micro and Teradyne formed a multi-year partnership to establish a semiconductor test and evaluation center at GSME’s new Silicon Valley headquarters.
proteanTecs and GUC are bringing embedded health and performance monitoring into GUC custom SoCs, extending earlier work around die-to-die links, HBM subsystems, and advanced packaging into the compute fabric itself.
NLM Photonics and SilOriX inked a joint PIC development agreement.

Fundings

Nexstrom raised $12M to commercialize a 300mm single-crystal 2D semiconductor platform.
MetaOptics secured an investment facility of up to $10M to expand in the U.S. and build a 300mm production line for metalenses used in optical interconnects, lidar and consumer devices.

Market forecasts

Yole expects the high-end packaging market to grow nearly fivefold to more than $51B by 2031, with AI infrastructure driving demand for technologies including hybrid bonding, CoWoS-L and CPO.
McKinsey raised its 2030 semiconductor market forecast to $2.3T, up 44% from its previous $1.6T estimate, with server and data-center chip revenue projected to reach $1.2T by 2030. McKinsey expects supply constraints, particularly for leading-edge chips and HBM, to persist for another 3 to 5 years.
The global DRAM module market generated $21.2B in 2025, up 59% year over year, reports TrendForce.

New Technologies
AI and accelerated compute

EdgeCortix introduced a chiplet-based physical-AI platform that scales from one to four compute dies.
Google is scheduled to launch a prototype satellite to evaluate how its TPUs perform in space.

Manufacturing, packaging and materials

Teradyne introduced Iris 100, an optical test platform for microLED arrays.
Brewer Science developed a high-temperature laser-release material for advanced-packaging temporary bonding/debonding.
ASM launched XP8 Vertos Flowable Carbon, a PECVD process that combines gap fill and self-planarization for high-aspect-ratio structures in advanced logic, DRAM and 3D NAND.
Cognex introduced an AI-based wafer and panel identification system for semiconductor manufacturing.

EDA

ChipAgents helped eMemory cut functional-model verification effort by 80% for its NVM IP using AI-driven verification automation.
As AI chips move toward stacked and chiplet-based architectures, EDA tools are being reworked for cross-domain analysis, faster exploration, and system-level design.

Mobile and edge

Samsung validated LPDDR6 on Qualcomm’s Snapdragon platform, extending the next-generation low-power memory technology toward increasingly demanding on-device AI workloads.
Qualcomm introduced two new 2nm premium mobile SoCs targeting on-device AI, gaming and imaging.

Photonics

Coherent launched PhotonLink, an integrated optics platform for AI data centers that combines InP lasers, VCSEL arrays, silicon photonics, specialty fiber, micro-optics and detectors with assembly and test.

Research
WashU researchers and collaborators demonstrated heterogeneous photonic integration of single-crystalline nanomembranes on silicon and silicon nitride.

A LANL/University of Pisa-led team reviewed how self-organizing networks of nanowires and nanoparticles adapt their electrical connections to process information and learn directly in HW. The approach could complement conventional computing by enabling energy-efficient, local AI in robots, autonomous vehicles and satellites. “We’re asking what becomes possible when the hardware itself is adaptive,” said co-author Adam Stieg of UCLA, pointing to AI that can operate and adapt locally.
Keysight is supporting UC Berkeley research on new over-the-air test methods for increasingly complex 6G devices and systems.

And:

Multi-kW Power Delivery Methods for Advanced 3D HI (UMN)
Concurrent Access to Host Memory & HBM to Accelerate LLM Inference (Georgia Tech, Nvidia)

Security
Hardware and firmware 

CERT/CC warned that vendor-signed UEFI Shell applications from multiple hardware vendors can be used to bypass Secure Boot and execute untrusted code before the operating system loads.

AI and cybercrime

An OpenAI agent accessed non-public files on an Australian Medicare statistics portal while performing an internal research task. Separately, researchers found evidence of multiple OpenAI agents coordinating attempts to access data from several Australian government sites.
Meanwhile, OpenAI called for international technical standards for frontier AI covering capability evaluation, human oversight, incident reporting, and automated AI research.
Microsoft disrupted EvilTokens, an AI-enabled cybercrime service linked to more than 12,000 compromised inboxes at over 10,000 organizations. Microsoft and its partners seized 50 websites and disabled more than 150 related domains.
Palo Alto Networks launched an agentic offensive-security service that uses Anthropic and OpenAI cyber models to continuously identify, validate, and help remediate exploitable attack paths.

Alerts

A hacking group claims it breached the FBI, stealing sensitive data, including FBI agents’ names, addresses, phone numbers, and information on their spouses. The FBI said it is “actively and aggressively investigating” the incident.
CISA released nine industrial control systems advisories this week. All the agency’s alerts for this week are here.
ENISA said cyber dependencies and supply-chain exposure are expanding the EU’s attack surface, with manufacturing accounting for 7% of recorded incidents. Its 2026 Threat Landscape also found more than 48,000 new CVEs in 2025, up 22%, and warned that AI is increasingly being used to support malicious operations.

Vehicles, Batteries
Automotive Deals & Products

Infineon launched its PSOC Control C3 Performance Line MCUs for real-time motor control and power conversion in automotive and industrial applications, with hardware acceleration and post-quantum security.
Mercedes-Benz signed a production agreement to integrate Wayve’s AI Driver into future vehicles starting within the next two years, bringing its embodied-AI driving system to urban and highway assistance.
Valens and onsemi are collaborating on a 3MP automotive image sensor with integrated MIPI A-PHY connectivity for high-volume camera applications.
Xpeng plans to offer more of its automotive technology to foreign carmakers, including electronic architectures, cockpit systems, Turing AI chips and ADAS software.
PATEO signed a strategic cooperation MoU with Arm to develop new solutions for physical AI applications, including next-generation AI-enabled workloads for automotive.
Microchip introduced two families of 65V energy-aware digital power monitors for 48V systems, including automotive applications.

EVs & AVs

A University of Florida team found that simple patterns of black-and-white stripes can disrupt camera-based depth estimation, potentially causing AVs to misjudge obstacle distances.
China’s Geely Auto Group says it has reached new performance heights in EV-charging technology, with its AI-powered chargers taking a vehicle from a 10% charge to 70% in 4 minutes 30 seconds.
Rally car driver Miko Marczyk set a world record for longest drive on a single EV charge, pushing an Audi A6 Sportback e-tron 1,338 kilometers across Poland on a single battery charge.
Bentley Motors unveiled its first EV, a luxury electric SUV called the Torcal.

Trending Video
Moving Test Data Faster: Options and workarounds for improving reliability in chips.
Increasingly complex chip designs require more test data than those developed at older nodes and on single planar dies. The challenge is moving all of that data through the system without slowing down the testing processes. Siemens EDA’s Vidya Neerkundar discusses the different test options, which ones work best where, and how different standards impact the test process.

Quantum
U. of Pavia, CEA-Leti and ST researchers developed a fully integrated quantum frequency processor on a silicon chip, combining quantum-state generation, frequency mixing, and programmable spectral control on a single silicon-photonics platform.
Microsoft made topological qubits built on its Majorana 2 chip available to DARPA for independent testing and evaluation at its new quantum research center in Maryland.
IonQ successfully tested an end-to-end real-time quantum error-correction decoder that runs on a single standard off-the-shelf CPU. In benchmarks simulating up to 408 logical qubits and more than 31.5M operations, the decoder added as little as 0.02% delay, according to IonQ.
In Germany, QUDORA will lead a 7-member consortium that has been invited to submit a full proposal for NFQC-1k, a roughly €122 million project to build a trapped-ion quantum computer with at least 1,000 physical and 50 logical qubits, plus a QPU pilot manufacturing line.

Workforce, Education
The University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign and Purdue University are teaming up to train semiconductor engineers. The partnership will focus on chip design, manufacturing, equipment, materials, testing, and advanced packaging through joint education programs and hands-on training.
The Trump administration directed agencies to consider recent or planned layoffs when reviewing H-1B cases and extended for another year the $100,000 payment requirement for certain H-1B workers seeking entry to the U.S.

New York announced $5M for a new STEM hub at Cicero–North Syracuse High School to prepare students for semiconductor and other technical jobs tied to Micron’s planned Central New York fab.
